why: The engine scores an off-field volatility term per side and nothing has ever supplied it, so `off_field` has been UNAVAILABLE on every game of every slate. This file is what makes the difference between the two answers the engine already distinguishes and EdgeDesk could not produce: `null` means NOBODY LOOKED, and `[]` means the configured sources WERE read and carried nothing material. The second is a real finding; the first is a gap. Without a registry there is no honest way to say the second, because nothing records what was supposed to have been read.
what_qualifies: A signal may move the confidence and volatility terms only if it is PUBLIC (a reader can open it), SOURCED (a named publisher and a URL), DATED (a publication timestamp, because the engine decays every signal on a 21-day half-life and an undated signal decays at a fixed 0.5 that describes nothing), and SEVERITY-GRADED (a number between 0 and 1 that a person assigned deliberately). All four. Three of four is refused.
why_empty: No keyless public feed EdgeDesk can read supplies all four. The availability layer answers a DIFFERENT question — who can play — and is never substituted for this one. A general news search returns headlines without severity and without a reliability a model may use; a paywalled wire supplies all four and may not be redistributed as a committed artifact. So this registry ships empty, deliberately, and the contract row says UNAVAILABLE rather than pretending a read happened.
how_to_populate: Add an entry per team key. `read_by` names the job or person that reads it and `cadence` says how often. Once a team has at least one entry, football/matchup/inputs.js will report an empty result as 'the configured sources were read and carried nothing material' instead of as a gap — so an entry here is a COMMITMENT that something actually reads it. Do not add a source nothing reads.
